analyst_view.overall: Early view: Córdoba, 10th, host an Oviedo side that will be playing only its second game under Raúl González, who one report says replaced Julián Calero on 9 November. Oviedo have one of the best away records in the division (13 points), while Iván Ania's Córdoba have won three of their last four league games and score regularly at El Arcángel.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, already high, and I agree. Oviedo's away games have been lively (2-1 at Cádiz, 2-2 at Almería, 2-1 at Ceuta) and Córdoba have scored in each of their last four league games, so a low-scoring game would be the surprise.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.4 corners, with 7.3 for Córdoba, which suits a team that attacks through crosses (Fran Escribá made stopping them his priority). I would not go higher than the site because Oviedo, strong away, will not simply sit back.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.6 cards. Córdoba ended a recent away game with nine men and Raúl has asked Oviedo for unconditional commitment, so the case for a high figure is there; I hold rather than go higher until the referee is named.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.6 shots, very high for this division. I lean lower: Oviedo's best away results have been compact ones (they led 2-0 at Cádiz and then held on), and Raúl's first weeks in charge are likely to put structure first, which caps the volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target. I lean slightly lower with the shots: Córdoba's crossing game produces many attempts, but headers from crosses often miss the target, and Oviedo's attack is without Chris Ramos (cruciate injury).
